title: Virginia pilots AI-assisted regulatory analysis, with savings attribution unresolved
summary: Vulcan Justinian analyzes Virginia regulations, but the reviewed reporting does not establish how much AI contributes to claimed economic savings.
account: Virginia’s Office of Regulatory Management commissioned a 2025 pilot of Vulcan’s AI-assisted regulatory analysis. Vulcan describes a system that maps legal provisions and drafts potential changes. VPM’s interviews with the company and the office’s director document a three-month, $150,000 contract and a process in which agencies review AI suggestions. VPM also distinguishes the state’s already-announced 25% regulatory reduction from the further reduction that officials intended AI to assist. The public reporting does not establish how much AI contributed to any economic savings. Researchers interviewed by VPM questioned whether reduced word or requirement counts demonstrated economic benefit. Statewide savings and housing-cost figures cannot establish money that Vulcan or AI saved. The date is the publication date of VPM’s report.
purpose: Assist agencies in analyzing legal authority, identifying overlapping provisions, and preparing proposed regulatory changes.
